entries.title: Acts 27:1
segments: As it was decided that we were to sail to Italy, Paul and some other prisoners were put in charge of a Captain of the Augustan Guard, named Julius.

entries.title: Acts 27:2
segments: We went on board a ship from Adramyttium, which was on the point of sailing to the ports along the coast of Roman Asia, and put to sea. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, went with us.

entries.title: Acts 27:3
segments: The next day we put in to Sidon, where Julius treated Paul in a friendly manner, and allowed him to go to see his friends and receive their hospitality.

entries.title: Acts 27:4
segments: Putting to sea again, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the wind was against us;

entries.title: Acts 27:5
segments: And, after crossing the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we reached Myra in Lycia.

entries.title: Acts 27:6
segments: There the Roman Officer found an Alexandrian ship on her way to Italy, and put us on board of her.

entries.title: Acts 27:7
segments: For several days our progress was slow, and it was only with difficulty that we arrived off Cnidus. As the wind was still unfavorable when we came off Cape Salmone, we sailed under the lee of Crete,

entries.title: Acts 27:8
segments: And with difficulty, by keeping close in shore, we reached a place called 'Fair Havens,' near which was the town of Lasea.

entries.title: Acts 27:9
segments: This had taken a considerable time, and sailing was already dangerous, for the Fast was already over; and so Paul gave this warning.

entries.title: Acts 27:10
segments: "My friends," he said, "I see that this voyage will be attended with injury and much damage, not only to the cargo and the ship, but to our own lives also."

entries.title: Acts 27:11
segments: The Roman Officer, however, was more influenced by the captain and the owner than by what was said by Paul.

entries.title: Acts 27:12
segments: And, as the harbor was not a suitable one to winter in, the majority were in favor of continuing the voyage, in hope of being able to reach Phoenix, and winter there. Phoenix was a Cretan harbor, open to the north-east and south-east.

entries.title: Acts 27:13
segments: So, when a light wind sprang up from the south, thinking that they had found their opportunity, they weighed anchor and kept along the coast of Crete, close in shore.

entries.title: Acts 27:14
segments: But shortly afterwards a hurricane came down on us off the land--a north-easter, as it is called.

entries.title: Acts 27:15
segments: The ship was caught by it and was unable to keep her head to the wind, so we had to give way and let her drive before it.

entries.title: Acts 27:16
segments: Running under the lee of a small island called Cauda, we only just managed to secure the ship's boat,

entries.title: Acts 27:17
segments: And, after hoisting it on board, the men frapped the ship. But, afraid of being driven on to the Syrtis Sands, they lowered the yard, and then drifted.

entries.title: Acts 27:18
segments: So violently were we tossed about by the storm, that the next day they began throwing the cargo overboard,

entries.title: Acts 27:19
segments: And, on the following day, threw out the ship's tackle with their own hands.

entries.title: Acts 27:20
segments: As neither sun nor stars were visible for several days, and, as the gale still continued severe, all hope of our being saved was at last abandoned.

entries.title: Acts 27:21
segments: It was then, when they had gone a long time without food, that Paul came forward, and said: "My friends, you should have listened to me, and not have sailed from Crete and so incurred this injury and damage.

entries.title: Acts 27:22
segments: Yet, even as things are, I urge you not to lose courage, for there will not be a single life lost among you--only the ship.

entries.title: Acts 27:23
segments: For last night an angel of the God to whom I belong, and whom I serve, stood by me, and said--

entries.title: Acts 27:24
segments: 'Have no fear, Paul; you must appear before the Emperor, and God himself has given you the lives of all your fellow-voyagers.'

entries.title: Acts 27:25
segments: Therefore, courage, my friends! for I believe God, that everything will happen exactly as I have been told.

entries.title: Acts 27:26
segments: We shall, however, have to be driven on some island."

entries.title: Acts 27:27
segments: It was now the fourteenth night of the storm, and we were drifting about in the Adriatic Sea, when, about midnight, the sailors began to suspect that they were drawing near land.

entries.title: Acts 27:28
segments: So they took soundings, and found twenty fathoms of water. After waiting a little, they took soundings again, and found fifteen fathoms.

entries.title: Acts 27:29
segments: Then, as they were afraid of our being driven upon some rocky coast, they let go four anchors from the stern, and longed for daylight.

entries.title: Acts 27:30
segments: The sailors wanted to leave the ship, and had lowered the boat, on pretense of running out anchors from the bows,

entries.title: Acts 27:31
segments: When Paul said to the Roman Officer and his men: "Unless the sailors remain on board, you cannot be saved."

entries.title: Acts 27:32
segments: Upon that the soldiers cut the ropes which held the boat, and let her drift away.

entries.title: Acts 27:33
segments: In the interval before daybreak Paul kept urging them all to take something to eat. "It is a fortnight to-day," he said, "that, owing to your anxiety, you have gone without food, taking nothing.

entries.title: Acts 27:34
segments: So I urge you to take something to eat; your safety depends upon it, for not one of you will lose even a hair of his head."

entries.title: Acts 27:35
segments: With these words he took some bread, and, after saying the thanksgiving to God before them all, broke it in pieces, and began to eat;

entries.title: Acts 27:36
segments: And the men all felt cheered and had something to eat themselves.

entries.title: Acts 27:37
segments: There were about seventy-six of us on board, all told.

entries.title: Acts 27:38
segments: After satisfying their hunger, they further lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.

entries.title: Acts 27:39
segments: When daylight came, they could not make out what land it was, but, observing a creek in which there was a beach, they consulted as to whether they could run the ship safely into it.

entries.title: Acts 27:40
segments: Then they cast off, and abandoned the anchors, and at the same time unlashed the gear of the steering oars, hoisted the foresail to the wind, and made for the beach.

entries.title: Acts 27:41
segments: They got, however, into a kind of channel, and there ran the ship aground. The bows stuck fast and could not be moved, while the stern began breaking up under the strain.

entries.title: Acts 27:42
segments: The advice of the soldiers was that the prisoners should be killed, for fear that any of them should swim away and make their escape.

entries.title: Acts 27:43
segments: But the Roman Officer, anxious to save Paul, prevented their carrying out their intention, and ordered that those who could swim should be the first to jump into the sea and try to reach the shore;

entries.title: Acts 27:44
segments: And that the rest should follow, some on planks, and others on different pieces of the ship. In these various ways every one managed to get safely ashore.
